observations: Photo 0: A metallic automatic transmission unit with an attached torque converter, sitting on a paved/brick floor outdoors.
A white label on the transmission case reads '460' with some smaller text above it that is too blurry to read fully.
Photo 1: Close-up of the torque converter bell-housing area, showing wear, oil residue, and gasket marks.
Photo 2: Side view of the transmission unit, with dark oil staining visible on the wall and floor behind it, suggesting a fluid leak either from this unit or nearby stored parts.
A semi-transparent watermark reading 'FIDEL AUTOS GLOBAL LIMITED' appears across all three photos.
No Mercedes-Benz logo, casting marks, or engine/transmission code (e.g., '722.9', 'M278', '1282') is legible in any photo.

claims.evidence: No part number, casting code, or Mercedes-Benz marking is legible in photo 0, 1, or 2; also M278 is an engine code (V8 biturbo), not normally paired with the G63 (which uses M157), creating an internal inconsistency in the seller's own description.
Shape and bell-housing style are consistent with a Mercedes-Benz automatic transmission, but no badge or stamped part number is visible to confirm make.
No video, bench-test clip, or fluid/operation evidence shown; claim is cut off and unsupported by any photo.

risks.risk: Internal wear or damage (clutch packs, valve body, torque converter lock-up clutch) cannot be assessed from exterior photos.
risks.proof: A video of the transmission being bench-tested or spun on a rig, or a borescope/teardown photo of internals.

risks.risk: Visible oil staining on the wall/floor near the unit suggests a possible fluid leak from a seal or case crack.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the transmission case and seals showing no active leak, plus a photo of the unit elevated off the ground away from the stain.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having a leak needing seal/gasket repair

risks.risk: Mismatch between stated engine code (M278) and stated vehicle (G63, which uses M157) raises doubt about correct application/compatibility.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the stamped part/casting number on the transmission case matching a verifiable Mercedes parts catalog entry.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unconfirmed-fitment, generic used transmission

risks.risk: Mileage, accident history, and reason for removal (engine swap vs. transmission failure) are unknown.
risks.proof: Seller statement with supporting donor-vehicle photo, mileage sticker, or VIN tag matching the removed unit.
risks.if_unproven: priced at worst case (unknown-condition used unit)

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the stamped part/casting number on the transmission case.
Photo or video of the donor vehicle (dashboard odometer, VIN plate) this transmission was removed from.
Video of the transmission being tested or confirmation of how 'worked perfectly fine' was verified.
Clearer photo showing whether the oil stain is from this unit or unrelated to it.
response.reason: The item cannot be confirmed as a Mercedes-Benz transmission from the photos (no legible badge or part number), and the comparable listings provided are all for Audi, Toyota, Honda, and Lexus gearboxes, none of which are a valid price reference for this claimed Mercedes unit.
